newsitem.title: USA: Rhode Island ratepayers face two pct hike Jan. 1.
newsitem.headline: Rhode Island ratepayers face two pct hike Jan. 1.

text.p: PROVIDENCE, R.I. (Dec 17) - Rhode Island utility customers will find their bills going up by about two percent on January 1, both public officials and utility spokesmen said on Tuesday.

Under the utility deregulation bill signed by Gov. Lincoln Almond in August, the Public Utilties Commission rate-setting review was scrapped and instead the utilities will be granted annual hike on a formula based on the Consumer Price Index (CPI).

Under the old regulatory system, Eastern Utilities Associates' Blackstone Valley Electric, which at peak supplies 270 megawatts, and Newport Electric, which supplies 100 megawatts at peak, would not have been granted any rate hikes as both were earning more than the the 11 percent profit limit set by the PUC in 1992.

Narragansett Electric, part of New England Electric System, which serves 325,000 customers, including 10,000 who qualify for low-income rates and has a peak load of 1,012 megawatts, was earning profits of almost seven percent.

The rate hike will provide Narragansett Electric with $10.8 million in additional revenue, Blackstone Valley $2.8 million and Newport Electric will get $1.4 million. "The only thing left for us to do is make sure they do the math right," said Adrianne Southgate, general counsel for the Rhode Island Public Utilities Commission.

Southgate said there has been debate about which CPI to use "Do you use the urban CPI, the national CPI, the Boston CPI?. This time around we're using the urban CPI, but a final decision will be made this spring," she said.
Todd McLeish, a spokesman for Blackstone Valley, said the rate hike would apply across the board to all of its 84,000 customers, including the 400 ratepayers who have low income status.
Rhode Islanders "had been told by their elected officials that their rates would be lowered by deregulation," said the PUC's Southgate.
McLeish said, "The lower rates will begin as soon as competition comes in." He said he expected competition to be fully completed by July 1, 1998.
